Okay... here is my thoughts on karma and shit posts:

To start, I agree, I never cared if it was my cake day. I never really cared if it was anyone else's either. However, I will admit that there were some times where some good OC came out of a cake day post. And that there is some validity in celebrating it.

But to farm karma? I agree, it seems dumb to judge someone on the amount of points they can collect. Yet, it does feel a little rewarding when you can get that kind of quality post, or make someone laugh, or do something to provide for the conversation. And this is where shit posts become important, or the over arcing concept of what makes shitposting good.

I would call it an art, an art I enjoy and one not easily executed or appreciated a lot of time, but an art none the less. Certainly there are bad shit posts, but there are bad serious posts, bad discussions, bad jokes, bad memes. Wherever there is content to had, there is content that is bad, but this is a good thing. It is what distinguishes the higher quality content from the lower quality content. And to bring this back to shitposting, quality shitposting is not necessarily derailing the conversation, but to insert an amount of absurdity into a discussion without breaking its flow. This is usually for comedic effect, and when done correctly, can enhance the conversation as well as address different ideas while introducing them in a more abstract, if not comical way. Bad shitposting is utilizing randomness to derail a conversation. I for one believe my shit posts are all intensive purposes for the prior, intelligently thought out responses that have some amount of wit, used to introduce an idea, a joke, or a concept, or to provide emphasis to the a ridiculous aspect of a concept or idea. Hell, it is why the primary amount of memes I like, use, and keep are those that are reactionary. Because on the internet you can't gauge someone's personal and emotive expression as well just through text.

I think shitposting is good. It offers a little cynism but with some humor, and when done right is there to poke fun at an issue, and shouldn't be intended to hurt an individual.

Hey guys! Voat newbie here, came from Reddit, and all I can say is that Voat is awesome!

Anyways, this is going to be my first post on /v/gamedev, and it's about a 2D game engine I've found on the web.

The engine is called Duality. I've found it while browsing the GitHub projects page. It was featured in there, and it got my attention.

It is a 2D game development framework, based (or powered) by C#. Currently, it supports Windows only. But in the near future, cross-platform may be possible.

Features

  • Plugin Architecture: Easily introduce game logic via plugins
  • Component Based Design: Allows your own code to blend in seamlessly
  • Base Infrastructure: Rendering, Audio, Physics, User Input, ...
  • Content Management: Takes care of all your game resources
  • Live Editing: Preview and Test directly in the editor
  • Hot-Reload Resources: Modified Assets are automatically reloaded
  • Hot-Reload Plugins: Write code and test it directly without restart
  • Modular Design: Tailor the editor exactly to fit your game

What makes it different from the other 2D engines?

Here's a comparison made by SirePi, a member of the Duality community:

  • Starting from scratch: you have an empty plot of land, there is a forest, some stone, and you have a few tools.
  • Low level frameworks (XNA, SFML, ...): you have some premade panels that you can arrange how you want to make a room, a forest, stone, some pre-cut lumber and materials, and some machines that help you do the work.
  • Duality: you have a room that you can stretch and reshape how you want, walls are already painted and the floor is down, but you can still paint over them or change the tiles. You have unlimited access to IKEA and to the woodshop if you so prefer. Lots of machines.
  • Others (Unity, ...): you can choose the room and furniture you want from a shiny catalogue, but the instructions on how to make your own are written in an obscure and forgotten language.

Links

  • Images: http://www.indiedb.com/engines/duality/images/duality-game-screenshots#imagebox
  • Community: http://forum.adamslair.net/
  • Homepage: http://duality.adamslair.net/
  • Download: http://dualitybin.adamslair.net/
  • Project Wiki: https://github.com/AdamsLair/duality/wiki
